notes.text: Jaylen Clark said at shootaround that without Anthony Edwards in the Timberwolves lineup the last couple of games, "guys' roles are naturally just expanding." He added: "We're definitely a better team with Ant." Clark said his job is to guard and hit open shots.

Deandre Ayton played seven first-half minutes and none after halftime in the Wizards' loss at Oklahoma City. Coach Brian Keefe: "Just a lower leg, a calf. Got hit in the calf. That's all I have for right now."

Draymond Green said Steve Kerr sat him and Stephen Curry for the first minute of overtime: "we're like, nah, we're good." The reserves went up 4. Green said the depth lets the Warriors manage minutes: "that's what we've been leaning into."

Stephen Curry and Draymond Green sat the first minute of overtime in the win over Orlando. Steve Kerr credited assistant Seth Cooper's plan to preserve them for the season: "it's not the old days." He expects both to play Monday but will see how they feel.

Anthony Black left the overtime loss at Golden State with a cramp, Sean Sweeney said. Jamal Cain had a double-double off the bench. "We have 3 of our most important guys down right now," Cain said. "Guys got to step up."

Houston wants Fred VanVleet's minutes around 30, Ime Udoka said after the loss to Phoenix. He played 19 in the first half. Asked if Amen Thompson was hurt after a shove under the basket, Udoka said he didn't see a limp: "I told him, you gotta be stronger than that."

"I feel good. I feel good. I was ready to play," Jalen Johnson said after logging 36 minutes in his return in the Hawks' win over Brooklyn. He said he will get treatment Sunday "and get ready for Monday."

Onyeka Okongwu left the win over Brooklyn. Quin Snyder said there was an adjustment period, "not wondering if you're going to have him." Aaron Wiggins said with bigs like Jock Landale and Asa Newell out, "we have to fill in as a team, and it has to be as a collective."

Mikel Brown Jr. will sit Sunday at Dallas; the Nets are holding him out of back-to-backs. "I'll obviously let you know when he does," coach Jordi Fernandez said. He said Brown's "body is where we want it to be" and back-to-backs bring "more risk."

Asked about heavy minutes, Miles Bridges said at Suns shootaround: "I really don't be feeling like I'm in game shape until after like the third game. So now I'm right where I want to be." On today's game: "Stopping Kevin Durant. Well, really stopping everybody."

Alex Sarr didn't really practice or work out over the summer because of a foot injury and is working his way back, Wizards guard Trae Young said Friday. Young called AJ Dybantsa, who missed the start of the season, a future star: "Now he's playing and trying to get his rhythm."

Victor Wembanyama tweaked his ankle again in Friday's road win, after doing the same against Dallas, and shook it off both times. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson credited his preparation and recovery work: "I think he also works on actually how he falls at times."

Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. tweaked his ankle and stayed in Friday's loss to the Spurs, a reporter said. Doug Christie said: "It doesn't surprise me." He added: "We were trying to make a run there, see how close we can get in. And it's like, okay, get him out of there."

Doug Christie said absences have kept the Kings from the lineup he wants: Ben Simmons went down early, and Keegan Murray and De'Andre Hunter were out in Friday's loss to the Spurs. On a set rotation: "It's difficult, man. I mean, to tell you it's not, I'd be lying."

Micah Nori said that even without Ja Morant, the Trail Blazers have "too many good decision makers" to turn it over 24 times. Those turnovers and 17 offensive rebounds allowed gave the Lakers 41 extra possessions in Friday's 124-118 loss, Nori said. Portland got 19.

Luka Doncic said he was tired after the Lakers beat Portland, but asked how he's holding up: "Feeling great." Asked if he can do it every night, he said "as long as we win, I'm good with whatever I do." On a Wilt Chamberlain comparison: "it's obviously a long season."

Joel Embiid wasn't on a minutes limit, Nick Nurse said, though the 76ers center played 25 minutes in Cleveland. Embiid on his shooting: "The way I'm jumping and... my hands... it's not what it used to be." On resting him Sunday, Nurse: "We have not discussed that at this point."

Dalen Terry played in Oklahoma City's win at Memphis on Friday. "It's good to see him in the uniform," Mark Daigneault said. "We're going to need him at some point." Asked about the shrinking bench, Jared McCain said: "We don't got that many players left out here."

Brayden Burries, asked after Friday's loss if he jammed his shooting hand: "Yeah. No, I'm good. I'm good." Pressed, the Bucks rookie said, "Yeah, I'm good." On handling 38 minutes, he said he tries to sleep more than eight hours, plus naps and ice on the road.

Morez Johnson Jr. says the shin is "going away" and he's "back to being bouncy." Dusty May said Johnson got out of shape missing practice but looks game-ready after the Mavericks beat Utah. Naji Marshall, back from illness, played longer spurts and wasn't tired late, May said.

Peyton Watson returned in the Cavaliers' win over the 76ers. Kenny Atkinson on what stood out: "Defense. Peyton Watson. Big difference." Atkinson praised Watson's defense on Maxey and said: "we got to make sure we're empowering him to bring the ball up."

Sam Merrill started Friday's win over the 76ers with Jarrett Allen out. "Yeah, it's bothering him," Kenny Atkinson said of Merrill's elbow. For Saturday, he said "we'll see." Atkinson said the Cavs "needed him out there to stabilize us."

Brandon Miller began limping in the second quarter of the loss to Boston and asked to come out. Charles Lee said the Hornets will evaluate him over the weekend and know more Monday. Lee called it a storm, adding: "I know we're on the verge of a breakthrough."

Adou Thiero is off the Lakers' injury report. JJ Redick on what he wants from Thiero's first reps of the season: "Defensive execution, game plan execution." Redick said Portland is "probably going to cross-match."
Yanic Konan Niederhauser is "coming back soon," Brandon Ingram said Friday. "We got some guys coming back soon," he added. Ingram is working back from heel surgery.

No target date for Brandon Ingram. The Clippers forward, recovering from heel surgery, said he's done some 3-on-3 and 5-on-5 and is "pretty close," but needs more 5-on-5 and to get comfortable jumping. "It's gonna take a little time, but I'll be ready soon."

Tyrese Haliburton and T.J. McConnell are out, and Kelly Oubre called Haliburton one of two "monumental pieces" Indiana must "Hold it down" for until they return. Oubre on playing Saturday against Denver: "Yes, sir." Pascal Siakam: "we started getting guys back already."

Nic Claxton was "full go" at Chicago Bulls practice after a G League stint. Coach Tiago Splitter said he'll "probably" play Sunday, on a minutes restriction "for sure, I believe." Claxton said nobody has told him the plan. Zach Collins is sick and missed practice.
Asked at practice Friday whether everyone but Steven Adams would be available Saturday at Phoenix, Rockets coach Ime Udoka said: "No, Clint," referring to Clint Capela.
Trey Murphy III, who missed the Pelicans' last game, said Friday ahead of tonight's game: "I feel pretty good, ready to play."

Santi Aldama is set to make his Mavericks debut Friday against Utah after surgery. Recovery ran longer than he expected, with no setbacks: "I feel really good right now." His role: "stretch the floor, knock down some shots" as Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg draw defenders.

Klay Thompson said he has no pain in his legs and credited the Heat training and coaching staffs for keeping him accountable: "I haven't felt this good to start a season in years." His first 30-point game in years, he said, gives him "so much confidence to keep going."

The Kings' Maxime Raynaud has no timeline for his knee: "I don't know yet." An X-ray and MRI ruled out a season-ending injury, he said. His everyday range of motion is back and he's on a day-by-day return plan, but isn't in basketball shape yet. He's at every practice.

"No, I'm not all the way back yet, man. I still don't have my pop." Sacramento Kings guard Malik Monk said he looks slow and a second late on tape after sitting out the preseason and the season opener. He said it isn't limiting him.
Dylan Harper on Victor Wembanyama rolling his ankle in the win over Dallas: "He's like, he's Superman. I mean, he rolls his ankle and pops right up and acts like nothing happened."

"Too many," Kings coach Doug Christie said of Darius Acuff Jr.'s 42 minutes against the Lakers: "I have to make sure that I protect him from himself." With no clear backup point guard, Malik Monk sometimes pairs with Domantas Sabonis so Sabonis runs the offense when Acuff sits.

DeMar DeRozan tried to shoot before Denver's win over Toronto, then "came back down and said he couldn't," Bryce Hopkins said. The rookie said J.J. Barea told him about 30 minutes before tip he'd play. "No 2-minute scouting report. I had to be locked in," Hopkins said.

Vit Krejci fractured his leg, "is what it sounds like," Micah Nori said after the win over Phoenix. He wasn't sure if it was leg or ankle and has no idea yet on surgery. He said Chris Youngblood will take those minutes and John Tonje or Jayson Kent will probably be called up.

Devin Booker went back in after Suns coach Jordan Ott made sure he was okay. Once the loss got out of hand, Ott said, "you got to save some for tomorrow" against rested Orlando in the first back-to-back. "We got to win the recovery battle right now," he said.

Suns coach Jordan Ott said missing the injured Mark Williams hurts the defense: "Mark's overall size deters rim attempts." He said the Suns now switch more, pulling their 5s off the rim. Defensive rebounding has surprised him: "I did think we would be bigger this year."

Adem Bona has neck soreness after a hit in the 76ers' win over Detroit. "He looks to be okay, but nothing official on that," Nick Nurse said. Joel Embiid hopes Dominick Barlow is "back soon." Tyrese Maxey said his right pinky has looked that way since last year: "I'm fine."

Cameron Johnson of the Denver Nuggets said he is fine after pulling up late in Monday's game. He said he figured it was a cramp and stood on the sideline the rest of the way to be safe: "hamstrings, they get a little tricky sometimes, but I'm fine."

"The circumstances aren't gonna change, you know, in the short term," Mark Daigneault said postgame of short-handed Oklahoma City, adding there will be no excuses. Bennett Stirtz, Aday Mara, Micah Peavy and Josh Dix are "getting an opportunity and they're delivering for us."

"We've been trying to reinvent ourselves since Anthony went down," Timberwolves coach Chris Finch said after the win. He wants LaMelo Ball "more aggressive" as a scorer and playmaker, and "he's done that." Late, Ball made "the right play after the right play," Finch said.

"I think he's playing through a lot of pain right now," Jazz coach Will Hardy said Wednesday of Lauri Markkanen. Hardy wouldn't commit to Markkanen's minutes at center: "Be a night-to-night thing." He said those lineups spread the court.

DeMar DeRozan was out for Denver's win over Toronto. On Aaron Gordon, David Adelman said: "we'd like to keep him at a threshold." Adelman said he ran Gordon longer in the first quarter with Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic. On Murray: "Jamal's played a lot."

Without Jayson Tatum for the first time this season, then without Payton Pritchard after he went out in the second half, the Celtics beat Milwaukee. Derrick White said they had no real point guard and were "running lineups that we haven't really done before."

Jalen Brunson can play 36 to 38 minutes, Mike Brown said after the Knicks beat Chicago. Brown said tracking in two-minute stretches shows Brunson doesn't fade. Brown won't push him: "It's going to impact him, in my opinion, come playoff time."

Jarrett Allen will be looked at Thursday after a knee-to-knee collision in the Cavaliers' loss to the Thunder. "Too early to determine," Kenny Atkinson said. Tyrese Proctor, starting for his defense on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, left with "a pretty good twist."

Isaiah Jackson will play for the Clippers: "He's good," Tyronn Lue said. Rui Hachimura and Derrick Jones Jr. are back. Lue said returning players are usually on minute limits, so he has to "juggle the times." He said the Clippers "need to cut some guys' minutes down."

Trey Murphy III is "more day to day" and is "going to be okay," Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley said before facing the Jazz. Dejounte Murray, back after time away for family, "will be back in the starting lineup," Mosley said.

Alex Caruso sat out Oklahoma City's win at Cleveland, but "he was in everybody's ear just talking like he always does," Micah Peavy said at shootaround. Peavy, who guarded Harden, Mitchell and Mobley, said: "I like to be that guy that coach can call on to guard those guys."

Yves Missi is "doing a little bit better," Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley said Tuesday. "He's able to get on the floor, get some standstill shooting, moving around a little bit," Mosley said, adding that Missi is "still not, you know, 100%."

Steven Adams is out with no timeline. Ime Udoka said that takes away Houston's favored double-big lineup, which he likes with Adams over Alperen Sengun and Clint Capela, but "gives other guys opportunity." Oscar Tshiebwe is a center option "if need be without Clint."

Steve Kerr said Jimmy Butler "would be my second choice when he's back" on Warriors technical free throws when Stephen Curry is off the floor. Kerr said Brandin Podziemski, Al Horford and De'Anthony Melton each missed one before Yaxel Lendeborg made one.

Max Strus returned in Monday's loss to the Raptors. "It was fun to get back out there and compete," he said. Strus said the Clippers have no reason to panic: "it's growing pains. We'll be all right." On his sharpness: "I'll just keep taking it day by day."

Tyronn Lue started Kris Dunn to help Darius Garland bring the ball up, but Dunn wore down too in the loss to Toronto: "To have him play 30 minutes in the back-to-back, that's not really fit for KD." Should Garland (back tightness) get a game off? "No, we'll take a look at it."

Max Christie left Monday's loss to the Kings with a reported hip injury and missed the second half. Dusty May said the Mavericks will evaluate him Tuesday and again "in the next couple days." Asked about Cooper Flagg grabbing his shoulder late, May said: "I didn't see that."

Morez Johnson Jr. scored 13 points in 17 minutes in the Mavericks' loss to the Kings. Asked about him postgame, Daniel Gafford said Johnson "has to, of course, pay attention to certain things when it comes to, I guess, his health, if I'm not mistaken."

Stephon Castle played through a migraine in the Spurs' last game, a random thing he said he has had a couple of times before. In the morning, "it was kind of bad, but as I came into the game, it got better," he said. Castle also said San Antonio is "still not at full strength."

With the Timberwolves "down some bodies," Chris Finch said he wants to get Jonathan Kuminga more chances to attack: "We'd be lost without him right now for sure." Ayo Dosunmu: "We short on guys right now." Kuminga had 10 rebounds and 4 blocks against Milwaukee.

Isaiah Stewart played a lot of minutes with Zach Edey in foul trouble, and Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo said Memphis has to be smart with him moving forward. "Some of the guys played very heavy minutes," he said, so the next practice will be handled carefully.

Rick Carlisle thinks a bruised knee made Kelly Oubre Jr. a last-second scratch, leaving Indiana with six players. Braden Smith's cramp was "not a pulled muscle or a strain as far as I know," he said. He said all six have earned "at least the consideration for more minutes."

Coby White knew his minutes number before tip-off in his first game back for the Hornets, and he thinks he went past it. "Probably played a little more than I was supposed to, actually," White said after the 124-91 loss to Detroit. He played a little under 16 minutes.

Franz Wagner said his knee is "all good" after he bumped it with Anthony Davis. On being lead creator with teammates out: "If you want to be a great player in this league, you can't shy away from that type of stuff." Desmond Bane said Wagner is "doing a hell of a job."
No Jock Landale and no Kingston Flemings for the Atlanta Hawks on Nov. 2, coach Quin Snyder said after the game.

Peyton Watson sat out the Cavaliers' loss to the Thunder. Kenny Atkinson said they're being cautious: "I'd rather him get, you know, fully healthy, you know, rather than throwing him out there game 6, game 7." Jaylon Tyson was also out.

Adou Thiero has had live exposures and is the only Laker not healthy, JJ Redick said Nov. 2: "Hopefully by the end of the week he'll be available." Ziaire Williams, back from a foot issue, is "not like on a minutes restriction," Redick said.

Darius Garland, Gradey Dick, Kobe Sanders, Brook Lopez and Kris Dunn were the Clippers' tentative starters for Nov. 2 because "the guys in their position ahead of them are out," Brian Shaw said. Asked about Brandon Ingram, he had "no update": "He's progressing."

Julian Champagnie said he thinks Utah's Lauri Markkanen will play against San Antonio on Nov. 2: "I think Markkanen is playing." Champagnie said Markkanen's return would change Utah's offense and who it runs plays for compared with the last meeting.

Rudy Gobert is sitting for the Timberwolves but travelled with the team. At shootaround he said he does not expect to be out long: "I don't plan to be on the sideline too much... that's why I really wanted to travel and be there with the guys."

Isaiah Hartenstein said OKC had three starters and a main bench player out for its two losses in Texas. "We lost probably some of our biggest defenders," he said, Chet Holmgren among them. On Micah Peavy: "anytime we can get a bigger wing out there, I think it's helpful."

Steve Kerr said Gui Santos sat the second half because his knee was bothering him, and Santos will also sit Nov. 2. "We'll reevaluate here over the next few days." The Warriors were already without Stephen Curry, Draymond Green, Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody.

Rookie Cameron Carr was available for his Lakers debut on Nov. 1 after a preseason injury, but coach JJ Redick would not commit to minutes or say whether he would play. "If he gets an opportunity... hopefully he shoots the ball well," Redick said.

Steven Adams and Reed Sheppard remain out for Houston, and Ime Udoka liked the response: "it felt good to see other guys step into those roles and us not really miss a beat." Fred VanVleet is coming off surgery; "we knew we wouldn't play back-to-back," Udoka said postgame.

Two guards out, and Memphis didn't know who until late after a tiring road trip. Coach Tuomas Iisalo's fix: Javon Small, who had barely played in the first five games, ran the second unit, and Cam Spencer played point with 13 assists and 0 turnovers.

No LeBron James and no Joel Embiid for the Philadelphia 76ers on Oct. 31, and no reason was given postgame. VJ Edgecombe confirmed both sat out and said the team's approach doesn't change: "every game matters, regardless of who's playing, who's not playing."

Dean Wade is "still coming out of this injury just a bit, but he knows how to play," 76ers coach Nick Nurse said postgame. Wade had 10 assists. Against two on the ball, Nurse said, he kept "finding that window and then making the next play."

Alperen Sengun returns for Houston. Ime Udoka, pregame, said the back flare-up came from taking a charge and tightening up: "there's no specific injury that continues to happen." Fred VanVleet is out, so Marcus Smart plugs in; with Sengun back, "we can be more well-rounded."

Dejounte Murray is out Oct. 31 "for similar reasons," Jamahl Mosley said before New Orleans' game, without saying what they are. On starting Jeremiah Fears with Herb Jones, Mosley cited Fears' pace and said Jones can "bring the ball up... orchestrate our offense a little bit."

Ja Morant is out, and Micah Nori says Portland will miss him on turnovers. He wants more from Scoot Henderson, attacking the rim, not settling for pull-ups: "we don't need him to orchestrate everything for everybody else, just for him to go."

Oso Ighodaro is back with the Phoenix Suns, and after the Oct. 30 loss Collin Gillespie said the offense flows easier with him: "you could kind of just give him the ball and he's like a point forward. And he's a really good connector."

"I know he's 2 for 9, but it's his first game back. I love that he shot 9." Denver coach David Adelman on Cameron Johnson's return. Spencer Jones is "hopefully coming back soon," he said, with no firm timeline. Alpha Diallo and Julian Strawther will return "at some point."

AJ Dybantsa says conditioning is the only thing holding him back after missing Washington's opening games: "just trying to get back in game shape." Two games in, coach Brian Keefe says he guarded Schroeder, Miller and Naz Reid: "He's a 2-way impact player."

Karl-Anthony Towns played Philadelphia with his wrist wrapped and said the injury predates it: "in the Bulls game for sure. That was when I did it." Asked if the wrist needs managing, no status was given: "that's something we'll deal with in the future."

Anthony Edwards has had surgery, which Bones Hyland called successful. After the Timberwolves' game on Oct. 30, Hyland said Edwards sent the team a 2-minute video urging Jaden McDaniels to "step up more, be a leader, be the voice of the team." No timeline was given.

Toronto Raptors' Scottie Barnes left late to have his arm checked after landing on an Orlando player's head on a missed dunk. Coach Darko Rajakovic said it's fine. Barnes said his arm and hand went numb: "It still hurts a little bit right now, but I think it'll get better."

"All available," Taylor Jenkins said of the Milwaukee Bucks. Kel'el Ware at center "has actually progressed to being something good for us," he said, though he wants more rim defense. Ware with Myles Turner? "At some point in the season. How soon, I can't predict."

Jordan Goodwin hopes Oso Ighodaro returns Oct. 30 and said at Phoenix Suns shootaround his absence hurt: "Being our point guard for that second unit. We play a lot through him." He'd open the floor for Collin Gillespie, Luke Kennard and him, and free Ryan Dunn to cut.

Caleb Martin is back for the Dallas Mavericks after rehabbing his hand, and Cooper Flagg liked what he saw after the game against Oklahoma City: "he's been... rehabbing his hand and trying to get back... But I thought he looked really good."

Portland felt Robert Williams III's absence in the loss to Memphis that ended a three-game winning streak, Deni Avdija said postgame. He gave no timeline for Williams' return: "First and foremost, we want him healthy and ready for games."

Dejounte Murray is out for New Orleans on Oct. 29, celebrating the birth of his son; Herb Jones starts. Jordan Poole (ankle) is out too, re-evaluated "in the next couple of days," Jamahl Mosley said. With both out, he wants Jeremiah Fears to be "a dominant point guard."

With Gui Santos out, Will Richard got his chance and was +13 at halftime off Golden State's bench on maybe one shot. Steve Kerr: "if everybody's healthy, you know, he's on the fringe of the rotation, but that's, that's his role."

Lakers guard Collin Sexton is still getting his legs back: "It's not the easiest coming back from injury." JJ Redick and Greg St. Jean told him to set the offense aside and "just go out and be a pest on defense." On Quentin Grimes going down: "That's our brother."

Terrence Shannon Jr. called Anthony Edwards, who is out, "the MVP of the league" and said everybody has to chip in. In the Timberwolves' loss, Jaylen Clark and Zyon Pullin got extended third-quarter minutes. "Whenever their name is called, I know they're ready," Shannon said.

Keyonte George said the Utah Jazz are losing Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic "for a little bit." His answer to the gap: "It's not just one person. It's not just me." He said the scoring and playmaking will be spread around.

Orlando's Tristan da Silva, with Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs out, expects a fairly quick adjustment: "It's bodies down... it's a lot on everybody, but that's not an excuse." He scored 20 for the first time this season; coaches stressed that turning down shots hurts the team.

From Chicago's postgame: Tobe Awaka, Patrick Williams and Nic Claxton, who hasn't played yet, were out; no new injuries. Zach Collins sat as Tiago Splitter went 10 deep. Collins is "a break in case of emergency," with minutes varying by matchup, even once Claxton returns.

Aaron Nesmith "seems to be doing well," Indiana's Rick Carlisle said, but the team still needs a few more players back: "we just need bodies." With a trip and a Nov. 1-2 back-to-back ahead, he told the roster "everybody's got to take care of themselves."

Obi Toppin played with his shooting hand splinted after jamming a finger, and Indiana's Rick Carlisle would only say he hopes it feels better by Oct. 30 in Miami. With Ivica Zubac out, Pascal Siakam said Larry Nance Jr. and Jay Huff have "big shoes to fill" and must rebound.

Jordan Poole went down against Denver and couldn't return, and Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley had no update: "As of right now, no, there's no really update." Losing Poole forced the second-half rotation: Saddiq Bey played over Jeremiah Fears because Mosley wanted size.

Austin Reaves "could beat you by himself," Tyronn Lue said Oct. 28, with Luka Doncic out for the Lakers. The Clippers coach expects Reaves to be the focal point and called him elite, crediting his growth to more playing time and a bigger role.

Dillon Brooks on his knee: "it was fine. It was a stinger." At Phoenix Suns practice he also went after officials: "I think refs talk and I think they have like a list of floppers." He said Oklahoma City flops without being called because of its pedigree.

Injuries have handed Josh Dix, the Thunder's two-way rookie, more playing time than two-way players usually get this early, he said at shootaround. With Cason Wallace, one of their "better point of attack defenders," out, Dix's job is spacing the floor and defending.

Not a minutes restriction, Micah Nori stresses, but Portland's coach wants Damian Lillard and Ja Morant around 30-32 minutes. On Morant, back from an injury layoff: "the game is starting to slow down for him... we are getting the best version of Ja Morant."

Boston's Jayson Tatum sat briefly late in regulation after banging knees with Julius Randle — "a little stinger." He still played 42 minutes on a back-to-back instead of resting after his Achilles injury, wanting to "be reliable like I was before I got injured."

Kneed in the leg guarding Paul George, Brooklyn Nets' Egor Demin watched the rest from the locker room but says "it's nothing serious... I think I'll be ready in a couple of days." Asked if it needs checking or he'll be good Oct. 30: "I have no idea. No idea."

Kneed in the leg guarding Paul George, Brooklyn Nets' Egor Demin watched the rest from the locker room but says "it's nothing serious... I think I'll be ready in a couple of days." Asked if it needs checking or he'll be good Oct. 30: "I have no idea. No idea."

Ausar Thompson returned for the Detroit Pistons in the Oct. 27 loss and fouled out, but J.B. Bickerstaff said they are monitoring his minutes, "especially coming into a back-to-back and those things, that we don't do too much too soon."

No timeline for Egor Demin's contusion from Nets coach Jordi Fernandez: "we'll see from there." Nolan Traore sat late with cramps despite wanting to play; Fernandez "had to save him from himself." Mikel Brown Jr. is on an undisclosed multi-week plan to build up minutes.

Jose Alvarado is out and being evaluated, and Knicks coach Mike Brown gave no timeline: "I don't know how long." Tyler Kolek takes on more. "He can't let pressure bother him or disrupt our offense at all," Brown said. On defense, "he's got to be a pest."

Patrick Williams is still out for the Chicago Bulls and Tobe Awaka rolled his ankle "a little bit" today, Tiago Splitter said. Isaac Okoro sat the second half as Splitter went bigger with Zach Collins for "more emphasis on our paint, on rebounding the ball."

With Kawhi Leonard out, RJ Barrett thinks he'll get more of the ball for the Toronto Raptors and wants his drives to collapse defenses into open shots for teammates. Next: two games against Orlando, who he said are "down 2 starters right now."

Kawhi Leonard is out for Toronto. Darko Rajakovic: "when Kawhi is not playing, obviously that's missing a very important piece, but that opens up a lot of opportunities for other guys." Asked if Ja'Kobe Walter keeps starting, he wouldn't commit: it depends on matchups.

"It is good that it wasn't anything super, super severe. You know, give him some time and he'll be back with us." Orlando's Desmond Bane on Jalen Suggs's injury, a view Jase Richardson shared. Neither gave a timeline for his return.

Charles Bassey is "working his way back after being off for about 2 weeks," Draymond Green said, and he and Al Horford manned Golden State's center spot: "I'm comfortable playing a 5." Veterans must hold the fort so undrafted rookie Graham Ike can grow, he said.

From Denver's media availability, on lost camp rhythm: "Cam being out, Spence having played a game." Cam: Cameron Johnson or Cam Whitmore, unspecified; Spence presumably Spencer Jones. DeMar DeRozan cited "a lot of injuries" and young players learning a defense new to him too.

Alex Caruso has an ankle sprain, and Thunder coach Mark Daigneault offered nothing more: "Ankle sprain. ... Nothing else." Missing key perimeter defenders, they started Kenrich Williams on Devin Booker, which Daigneault said "set an important tone."

With Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace out, Ajay Mitchell scored a career high for the Thunder: "I knew I'd probably have to come out and be even more aggressive." Isaiah Hartenstein said coaches must rework defenses without the pair's versatility.

Kevin Durant sat the whole fourth quarter at his own urging. "Kevin was like, let that unit roll," Houston's Ime Udoka said postgame. Fred VanVleet, Reed Sheppard, Tari Eason, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Sengun "got stops, got out and ran." Udoka still wants his minutes down.

Sergio de Larrea left in the second quarter and gets imaging Oct. 27; no timeline. Mavericks coach Dusty May: "I don't know what it is... obviously concerned because he's such a tough kid." Walter Clayton Jr. stepped in after a stay-ready game earlier that day.

Anthony Davis was hit in the hand during the Wizards' game on Oct. 26, and coach Brian Keefe had "no update yet" on his status. Trae Young wants better spacing from Alex Sarr and others around Davis: "We just got to get into our spacing better when AD got us in iso."

Justin Champagnie is being evaluated for a right foot injury. Wizards coach Brian Keefe would not say whether X-rays were taken or came back negative. Trae Young spoke of Champagnie's "recovery": "We gonna make sure he's right and we'll hold down the fort while he's gone."

Kon Knueppel, Coby White and Grant Williams are "making positive steps in all their rehab plans," Charlotte coach Charles Lee said, some further along than others. No timeline yet. Their absence means a bigger role for Christian Anderson: "mistakes are going to happen."

Otega Oweh's roster spot had to be used, but the Thunder are still "really working closely with him on his rehab," GM Sam Presti said. Calling injuries "easily the worst part of the job," Presti said this group has a different identity and must find its strengths.

Yves Missi is still out for the Pelicans, with "no updates just as of yet," Jamahl Mosley said. DeAndre Jordan said he, Karlo Matkovic, Derik Queen and at times Zion Williamson will "hold down the fort until he's back," which has changed the rotations quite a bit.

Nick Nurse thinks four or five of the 76ers' power forwards and centers are out. Interior defense without Joel Embiid has "been a little bit of a concern"; Jabari Walker, Dean Wade, LeBron James and Adem Bona have all tried there. Of Bona: "the first game he's impacted."

"I know we thin, so we all got to come in and rebound." With Jalen Duren and Ausar Thompson out, the Detroit Pistons' Daniss Jenkins said after the Oct. 25 game that rebounding falls on everyone. He did his part with 8 rebounds.

Ivica Zubac's ankle X-rays were negative for a fracture, but it's swollen and Rick Carlisle called him "pretty unlikely" to play Oct. 26, "but we'll see." Ben Sheppard is unavailable and T.J. McConnell isn't back. Jay Huff and Larry Nance Jr. did "a terrific job" filling in.

Back from tendonitis on a minutes cap, Golden State's Charles Bassey said he had no problems and could have played much more: "you guys should be expecting to see more of me." Steve Kerr said Georges Niang, out about a year injured, "doesn't have his legs underneath him yet."

Bub Carrington was not injured when he left the Wizards' bench during their previous game, coach Brian Keefe said. Asked whether Carrington was sick, Keefe would not say: "was not injured. ... That's all I have for you."

Down Mark Williams and Oso Ighodaro, the Phoenix Suns are using Ryan Dunn and Miles Bridges at center sooner than planned. Coach Jordan Ott called rebounding the challenge when they go small. He didn't think Collin Gillespie grabbing his left hip was anything.

Nate Ament made his NBA debut for Milwaukee after weeks out injured, crediting "the medical staff here and the team I got around me" for getting him back to 100%. He wanted to guard Jaylen Brown: "I wanted that challenge." On his early fouls, he's learning to be smarter.

With Oso Ighodaro out, the Phoenix Suns' Khaman Maluach said he and Duop Reath "both got to stand up for Oso" but he won't change his game: "It's not like, oh, Oso's out now, let me take a bunch of shots or bad shots, you know."

From Golden State's media availability: Brandin Podziemski was relayed as saying he won't play Oct. 24. Yaxel Lendeborg "should absolutely be playing" in his first back-to-back and must be "way more aggressive" without Stephen Curry. Steve Kerr hasn't decided whether Curry rests.

Zach LaVine on Domantas Sabonis's return for the Sacramento Kings: "it was good to see him back and healthy," calling him the engine of their first half against Portland. Then: "The 3rd quarter is killing us." Portland was back in it within five minutes of halftime.

Deni Avdija played a lot of minutes out of necessity, Portland coach Micah Nori said postgame: "The good news is we have 3 days off for him to recover." A small lineup with Sidy Cissoko and Toumani Camara also kept Robert Williams III's minutes "down where we wanted them."

Zach Edey is back from rehab, and Memphis Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo says "he's gotten more athletic" during it, crediting the medical and performance staff. Rookie Cam Boozer shows no sign of fatigue, Iisalo said, "so we got to be smart there."

"So thankful to be healthy," said Walker Kessler, who played 5 games last season and, 2 games into this one, joked he expects to pass that total. The Lakers center had 6 blocks and 3 steals but doubted the count: "I think they were pretty generous with the blocks."

Jake LaRavia was ruled out with an ankle injury after testing it at shootaround and in the treatment room. "It's not there," Lakers coach JJ Redick said. LaRavia, who played all 82 games last season and set doing it again as a goal, hopes to return Oct. 25, if not Oct. 27.

Oso Ighodaro has an oblique strain and is out for Phoenix's next game, but coach Jordan Ott said "we hope it's just more day-to-day than long-term." Luke Kennard practiced, "trending in the right direction." Khaman Maluach will "probably" see more possessions, Ott said.

Chet Holmgren and Jaylin Williams have moved to power forward, Holmgren said after Oklahoma City's Oct. 22 win: "we got other centers out there." He named Aday Mara, Isaiah Hartenstein and Thomas Sorber, the last "when he comes back." No timeline for Sorber.

Kristaps Porzingis is not with the Warriors, and Stephen Curry said he hasn't spoken to him since training camp started. He called it hard on Porzingis and the team: "It is a tough one to figure out for the now, for the future... you would have loved to have him here."

Asked at Orlando Magic practice how his shoulder was feeling, Franz Wagner gave a one-word answer: "Good." Sean Sweeney on Anthony Black: "Full participant and working hard, shooting jumpers right now. Looks good and making them all."

The Celtics' Mitchell Robinson says getting hurt "not really" affected him: "feel it a little bit here and there, but shit happens." On his last game: "obviously one of the best defensive bigs in the league and I didn't show it." He left Joe Mazzulla's last text unanswered.

Without T.J. McConnell and Aaron Nesmith, Indiana is "mixing and matching with certain guys," Rick Carlisle said. From the postgame: the aim was to "keep one of our main point guards as the point guard the whole game," so Tyrese Haliburton and Jrue Holiday shared less time.

GG Jackson missed "over a week" of practice before the opener, and Tuomas Iisalo said it showed: the Grizzlies' bench of Jackson, Jerami Grant, Scotty Pippen Jr., Quinten Post and Cam Spencer got winded, "even the shorter subs, like 4 or 5 minutes."

Spencer Jones is "full go" for the Nuggets' opener, David Adelman said, minutes pending trainers. Christian Braun, hurt all offseason, probably feels freest since last year's Clippers game. Aaron Gordon is healthy: "When Aaron plays, we're as good as any team in the league."

"I have a few things that I know he doesn't really like, so I'm going to try to apply them. Can't tell y'all what it is though." — Bennedict Mathurin, facing Tyrese Haliburton for the first time in his Pelicans debut against Indiana. Haliburton is back and "healthy," he said.

"I basically didn't play for a whole year," Jalen Williams said after the Thunder's opener, but he expects a "pretty quick adjustment" and called his defense already great. Jared McCain, also back from injury: "When I was injured, it was just like the worst time ever."

Ben Simmons is out with no timeline, so Doug Christie changed his rotation plan. The Kings won't ask Malik Monk or Nique Clifford alone to replace his playmaking: "it's not going to be one person." Dylan Cardwell and Maxime Raynaud weren't with the team; everyone else is active.

"Everyone full, fully available," Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins said ahead of Game 1. Parting with Kevin Porter Jr. was "a very difficult decision," to open pathways for young guards. Brayden Burries gets early on-ball chances; he and Kasparas Jakucionis must grow as playmakers.

Precious Achiuwa, ready for the Sacramento Kings' season after "sitting out for a long time," says scoring isn't his job: "I don't really care offensively. It's just my job here is to make these guys better." Top priority: get Zach LaVine going early, and Darius Acuff Jr. too.
Jase Richardson "made some shots, was moving pretty good" at Orlando's practice, Magic coach Sean Sweeney said: "He did a good job." Jonathan Isaac was out practicing as well, Sweeney said.

"It's just sad to see, 'cause you put in all that work to get back." Clippers coach Tyronn Lue on Ben Simmons, who he said had done the work and looked healthy. Asked about inactive Bradley Beal and Johnni Broome, he gave no statuses: "I think the guys are looking good."

Sam Merrill went through all of Cleveland's practice, scrimmaging included — "really good news," Kenny Atkinson said. Nae'Qwan Tomlin, who had earned a rotation spot, is out for a stretch with no return date; his spot goes to the "best player," not a like-for-like swap.

Branden Carlson still has concussion headaches and isn't 100%, Portland coach Micah Nori said, adding Carlson has had one before: "So hopefully he will be okay." Chris Youngblood tweaked his Achilles but practiced a little. Micah Potter is still working back from an illness.

"Nate Bittle is out of the boot, so he's reconditioning now," Toronto's Darko Rajakovic said at practice, calling the team in "pretty good health." Asked whether Alijah Martin had tweaked his knee, he said Martin went through a whole practice and "was completely fine."

Adou Thiero and Cameron Carr missed Lakers practice again, JJ Redick said; Bronny James and Dalton Knecht had excused absences. Collin Sexton was "in practice, full participant," though Redick did not say whether he will play in the next game.

Asked for an update on Josh Hart, Knicks coach Mike Brown answered for the whole roster: "Yeah, no, no, everybody's healthy. Nobody was held out of any portion of practice." He did not address Hart individually.

Jalen Smith will start at center for the Bulls with Nic Claxton out, Tiago Splitter said, with Tobe Awaka "just coming back." Splitter wants everyone but the shooter chasing misses 75% of the time, up from about 40%: "we don't have the best shooting team in the NBA."

Cleveland's Kenny Atkinson said Nae'Qwan Tomlin sat out practice and Sam Merrill was limited; Khalifa Diop is "coming back from a setback." Atkinson wants a 10-man rotation, likely named only at game time: "I've made that mistake before... the guy tweaks an ankle."

T.J. McConnell (hamstring) isn't back yet and a couple more Pacers are still getting healthy, per Indiana's media availability. Quenton Jackson has run the bench at point guard; Rick Carlisle says he's "ready for... being a full-time roster guy and being ready at all times."

Joel Embiid is "ready to go" for the 76ers' opener, Nick Nurse said: "Some of those things weren't going on a year ago." Dean Wade, Dominick Barlow and Tacko Fall did not practice. Wade wore a practice jersey anyway. "Shouldn't make any judgments by those jerseys," Nurse said.

"I feel good. You know, just taking it day by day," said Anfernee Simons, who has missed 76ers practices over the past week. With no preseason game reps, he expects to "find my way" over the first 20 games. Asked if he'll play in the opener: "I can't confirm or deny that."
